EC Florida site Operational Extreme Current velocity [m/s] 1.7 2.6 Significant wave height [m] 2 6 Final Technical Report 30/57 Peak period [s] 7.5 13.27 Wind speed [m/s] 7.7 18 Table 7-2 Environmental conditions for the external Florida mooring system design The proposed design consists of three 70 mm polyester lines (lines 1 and 2 with 25 m in length and line 3 with 30 m), two of which come out of each hull to connect at an intermediate node, and the third line connects this node to a surface buoy. The net buoyancy of this surface buoy should be sufficient to withstand the weight of the catenary chain under operating conditions. This surface buoy is connected to the seabed using a 40 mm stud link chain of 770 m. The chain length has been set to avoid vertical uplift forces in the anchor point. 7.3 Jack-Up Mooring System For river and estuary deployments, MTV incorporates four jack-up legs that rest on the seabed and elevate the MTV slightly above the water surface. The four legs are located at the four corners of the vessel, each with a footing to allow for better support. The rising and lowering of the platform is done hydraulically, and this mooring system allows jacking-up in sites with depths up to 13 m. The proposed jacking towers would be welded to the hull and incorporate 4 hydraulically active gearboxes. The system is shown in Figure 7-5.
